theTwoQuestionsForTheTester: What the pod took with it (lostClaims, the gone-pod report): the members of the round who neither answered nor left having answered. Membership is update_round = R or update_left_round = R, so it survives a claim leaving, and a role first started in the replacement pod is no member.

Whom the replacement waits for (waitingClaims): every blocking claim that has not answered and has not left. Deliberately conservative and unchanged in spirit, because a claim the round has not asked yet still holds the pod and is asked at the next tick. TestPodUpdateAbortsTheReplacementForAClaimTheGroupNeverHeld is the lock on that and was not weakened.
trickyParts: The architect chose the record's shape after I put two to it: the round's own table, or the round's own columns on the claim. Shape B was chosen with four conditions, all met: the column records the round left and whether it had answered rather than a bare flag; only the round's end clears the columns; the report reads the members who neither answered nor left having answered; and the replacement's question stays conservative with its test unweakened.

A claim keeps its update_round when it leaves. That is what makes membership survive the leaving, and it is why the report can tell a claim whose end has already landed (neither field names R) from one that left mid-round (update_left_round names R).

Making both of sendPending's drops one shape has one deliberate consequence: a left round's ask is no longer dropped while no connection is registered or while a prompt's turn is awaited; it is dropped at the next send attempt. Nothing is sent meanwhile, and the round's own end drops it in any case.

The merge's one silent conflict had no marker: podupdate_fleet_test.go's rig posted a completion with a commit and no handoff record, which main's #2354 route now refuses HANDOFF_RECORD_REQUIRED. The rig now writes the phase's handoff record under the claim's own session, as dispatch handoff-write does, with the same call sites and the same assertions.
